content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., post-77+ peaks, model jumps to 79+ but true settles at 78+).
- Underestimate downward moves when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.10 to -0.30) — model often fails to fully reflect bearish sentiment.
- Overreact to short-term sentiment shifts: if sentiment turns positive after a dip, model may overshoot upward too quickly.
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect from recent highs/lows — true price often reverts to 1-2% below or above forecast peak/trough.
- Lagged response to sentiment: model reacts 1-2 days after sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment is negative — forecast lags true price by 1-3 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic when sentiment is consistently negative over last 18 days — reduce forecast by 1-2% for each -0.10+ sentiment unit.
- Avoid “sudden spike” forecasts when sentiment is flat or mildly negative — true price rarely exceeds forecast by >3% unless sentiment turns sharply positive.
